headings: Leave Policy

1. Purpose
Define eligibility, accrual, usage, carry-forward, encashment, and approval rules for all leave types so that managers, employees, and automated systems apply consistent rules.

2. Scope
Applies to all locations (Bengaluru, Mumbai, Delhi, Hyderabad) and all employment classifications listed in Section 4. Does not apply to third-party vendor personnel unless a separate written agreement incorporates these rules.

3. Definitions
| Term | Definition |
|------|------------|
| Annual Leave (AL) | Paid time off accrued for rest and personal needs |
| Casual Leave (CL) | Short-notice leave for personal exigencies |
| Sick Leave (SL) | Leave for personal illness or medical appointments |
| Maternity Leave | Leave related to childbirth as defined in Section 7 |
| Paternity Leave | Leave for the non-birth parent as defined in Section 7 |
| Compensatory Off | Time off in lieu of approved extra hours |
| Leave Year | 1 April – 31 March (aligned with Financial Year) |

4. Eligibility and Employment Classifications
| Classification | AL Accrual | CL | SL | Notes |
|----------------|------------|----|----|-------|
| Full-time permanent | Yes | Yes | Yes | Standard entitlements below |
| Part-time permanent | Pro-rata AL | Yes (pro-rata) | Yes (pro-rata) | Based on contracted FTE |
| Probationary | Accrues but usable only after confirmation except SL | Limited CL | Yes | See POL-HR-002 Probation |
| Intern | No AL | 3 days CL total | 3 days SL total | Fixed for internship duration |
| Contractor | Per contract only | Per contract | Per contract | Not governed by this policy unless incorporated |

5. Annual Leave (AL)
### 5.1 Entitlement
- Full-time permanent employees: **18 working days** per Leave Year.
- Accrual: 1.5 days per completed calendar month of service.
- New joiners: Pro-rata from joining date; first accrual credited at end of joining month if joined on or before the 15th, otherwise from next month.

5.2 Carry-Forward
- Maximum carry-forward into next Leave Year: **8 days**.
- Excess above 8 days lapses on 31 March unless an exception is approved in writing by CHRO before 15 March.

5.3 Encashment
- Encashment is permitted only on separation (resignation, retirement, or termination) for unutilized AL up to the carry-forward cap + current-year pro-rata balance.
- Encashment rate: Basic salary / 30 × number of days.
- No mid-year encashment while in service.

5.4 Approval Authority for AL
| Duration | Approver | Alternate if Approver Unavailable |
|----------|----------|-----------------------------------|
| 1–3 consecutive working days | Direct Manager | Skip-level Manager |
| 4–10 consecutive working days | Direct Manager + HR Manager acknowledgment | Department Head |
| >10 consecutive working days | Department Head + HR Manager | CHRO |

6. Casual Leave (CL)
- Entitlement: **12 days** per Leave Year for full-time permanent employees.
- Maximum continuous CL: 3 working days.
- Does not carry forward; unused CL lapses on 31 March.
- Approval: Direct Manager (or Skip-level if Manager unavailable). Same-day CL requires telephonic/email notification before shift start plus system entry within 24 hours.

7. Sick Leave (SL)
- Entitlement: **12 days** per Leave Year.
- Medical certificate required for SL of 3 or more consecutive working days.
- Does not carry forward.
- Approval: Direct Manager; HR must be informed for absences >3 days.

8. Maternity and Paternity Leave
- Maternity Leave: 26 weeks for the birth parent (as per applicable Indian law framework for the synthetic policy design). Application to HR at least 8 weeks before expected delivery where foreseeable.
- Paternity Leave: 5 working days within 3 months of childbirth. Approval: Direct Manager + HR notification.

9. Compensatory Off
- Granted only for pre-approved extra hours on weekends or public holidays, documented by Manager.
- Must be utilized within 60 days of the extra work date; otherwise lapses.
- Approval: Same as AL for the corresponding duration.

10. Public Holidays
- Published annually by HR before 15 March for the next Leave Year.
- Locations may have limited local holiday variations approved by CHRO.

11. Leave During Notice Period
- AL may be availed during notice only with written approval of Department Head and HR Manager.
- Company may require the employee to remain available; unapproved absence during notice may be treated as leave without pay or misconduct under POL-HR-005.

12. Exceptions
- CHRO may grant exceptional leave (paid or unpaid) for documented extraordinary circumstances. All exceptions must be recorded with reason and duration.

13. Compliance Monitoring
- HR runs monthly leave-balance reconciliation.
- Managers are responsible for timely approval or rejection (SLA: 3 business days for planned leave).

14. Consequences of Non-Compliance
- Unauthorized absence may be marked Leave Without Pay and, if repeated, may initiate disciplinary process under POL-HR-005.

- Full-time employees: 40 hours per week, Monday–Friday.
- Core hours (all locations): 11:00–16:00 India Standard Time — employees must be available for meetings and collaboration unless on approved leave.

- All employees must record attendance via the approved HR system or biometric device where installed.

- Fully remote arrangements require written approval of Department Head, CHRO, and (for roles with customer data access) CISO.
- Remote employees remain subject to the same leave, conduct, and security policies.

- Individual Contributors in non-exempt categories (as classified by HR): pre-approved overtime compensated as Compensatory Off (see POL-HR-001) or as per applicable wage rules.

headings: Policy Governance and Precedence

1. Purpose
Define how policies are created, approved, versioned, superseded, and how conflicts between documents are resolved.

2. Policy Lifecycle
1. Draft created by owning department.
2. Review by Legal/Compliance for conflict and clarity.
3. Approval by designated Approver Role.
4. Publication with Effective Date; prior version marked Superseded with Effective-To date.
5. Periodic review by Review Date.

3. Precedence Hierarchy (Internal Documents)
When two internal documents conflict:
1. **Currently effective Approved policy** of the higher authority (CEO/Board > C-level policy > Department policy).
2. More specific policy controls over general policy for the same subject.
3. Later Effective Date controls over earlier if both Approved and overlapping.
4. SOP cannot override Policy; SOP implements Policy.
5. Draft, Retired, or Archived documents have **no operational force**.

4. External Law vs Internal Policy
Genuine legal or regulatory obligations (where verified) take precedence over internal policy. Internal policy may be stricter than law but cannot authorize non-compliance with applicable law. This dataset contains **synthetic internal controls** and does not invent statutory text. For real-world legal questions, qualified legal counsel is required.

headings: Access Control and Data Classification Policy

1. Purpose
Define data classification levels, access principles, authentication requirements, and rules for granting, reviewing, and revoking access.

2. Data Classification Levels
| Level | Definition | Examples | Access Rule |
|-------|------------|----------|-------------|
| Public | Approved for external release | Marketing website, published job ads | No restriction |
| Internal | Standard company information for employees | Org charts, internal wikis, non-sensitive policies | Authenticated employees |
| Confidential | Sensitive business or customer data | Customer contracts, financial forecasts, HR records | Role-based + business need; Manager or data-owner approval |
| Restricted | Highest sensitivity | Credentials vaults, M&A materials, security incident details, production secrets | Explicit named authorization by data owner + CISO (or delegate); time-bound |

3. Authentication
- All systems: unique user ID; multi-factor authentication (MFA) mandatory for remote access and for any system containing Confidential or Restricted data.
- Privileged accounts: separate admin IDs; MFA; session logging; quarterly access review.

4. Access Grant Principles
1. Least privilege.
2. Need-to-know.
3. No standing access to Restricted data without active ticket and expiry date (max 90 days, renewable).
4. Joiner: access provisioned per role template within 1 business day of start after Manager confirmation.
5. Mover: previous access reviewed within 3 business days of role change.
6. Leaver: all access revoked by end of last working day; privileged access revoked at notification of departure.

5. Confidential Finance Document Access Example
An employee may access a Confidential Finance document only if:
- Their role is in Finance, ELT, or a specifically authorized project role; **and**
- There is a documented business need; **and**
- Access is approved by the data owner (typically Finance Director or CFO) or via an approved role template; **and**
- The system enforces MFA and audit logging.

6. Prohibited Actions
- Sharing credentials.
- Storing Restricted data on personal devices or unapproved cloud services.
- Using unapproved AI tools with Confidential or Restricted data (see POL-AI-001).

headings: SOP — Leave Application and Approval

1. Purpose
Provide ordered steps for employees and managers to request, approve, or reject leave in compliance with POL-HR-001.

2. Trigger
Employee needs time off under any leave type defined in POL-HR-001.

3. Preconditions
- Employee has active HR system account.
- Sufficient balance exists for the leave type (system-validated) or exception path is used.

4. Responsible Roles
| Step | Role |
|------|------|
| Submit request | Employee |
| First approval | Direct Manager (or alternate per POL-HR-001) |
| Acknowledgment / second approval | HR Manager or Department Head when required by duration |
| Balance update | HR system (automated) |

5. Ordered Steps
1. Employee opens Leave Request in HR system; selects type, dates, partial-day if applicable, and comments.
2. System checks balance and policy rules; blocks submission if balance insufficient unless exception flag is raised.
3. Request routes to Direct Manager.
4. Manager approves or rejects within **3 business days** (planned leave) with comments.
5. If duration requires second approval (see POL-HR-001 Section 5.4), request routes to Department Head / HR Manager.
6. On final approval, balance is decremented; calendar is updated; employee and Manager receive confirmation.
7. On rejection, employee is notified with reason; no balance change.

6. Decision Branches
- **Same-day Casual Leave:** Employee notifies Manager before shift start; enters system request within 24 hours; Manager confirms.
- **Manager unavailable:** Request escalates to Skip-level Manager after 3 business days or immediately if marked urgent.
- **Insufficient balance:** Employee may request unpaid leave; requires Department Head + HR Manager approval.

7. Completion Criteria
Approved or rejected status in HR system; employee notification sent; audit log entry created.

8. SLA
Manager decision: 3 business days for planned leave. HR acknowledgment when required: 2 business days.

CHRO-approved exceptions per POL-HR-001 Section 12; recorded with reason code.

After documenting existing controls, residual likelihood and impact are assessed; residual score = residual likelihood × residual impact.

headings: AI Usage and Governance Policy

1. Purpose
Govern the use of artificial intelligence tools and models so that Asterion benefits from AI while protecting data, customers, and decision integrity.

2. Approved Use Cases
- Internal knowledge retrieval and policy Q&A (RAG systems such as Asterion AI Assist) with citation of sources.
- Code assistance for developers on non-Restricted codebases using approved tools.
- Drafting of internal documents with mandatory human review before external or decision use.
- Analytics feature assistance where outputs are validated against source data.

3. Prohibited Use Cases
- Inputting Restricted data into any non-approved external AI service.
- Fully automated decisions that grant access, approve spend above policy thresholds, hire/fire, or modify production security controls without human approval.
- Generating content presented as factual company policy when no supporting document exists.
- Using AI output as the sole evidence for compliance or audit without human verification.

4. Human Review Requirements
| Output Type | Review Requirement |
|-------------|-------------------|
| External customer communication | Mandatory human approval |
| Policy interpretation for action | Human confirmation against source policy |
| Financial figure or approval recommendation | Human verification against POL-FIN-003 and source data |
| Security or access change recommendation | CISO or delegate approval |

5. Evidence vs Instructions
Retrieved documents and passages are **evidence**. They do not override system authorization, approval workflows, or security controls. AI systems may recommend actions; they must not bypass authorization or independently execute prohibited operations.

6. Hallucination and Gap Reporting
Users and operators must report suspected hallucinations or missing-policy answers through the designated feedback channel. AI systems must state when available information is insufficient rather than invent policy.

Limitations and Future Work
**Project:** SYNAPTIX-PM-2023-2025

Limitations
1. **Acoustic data scarcity** — EXP-PM-006 demonstrated that acoustic-only models suffer from high false-positive rates when labeled failure events are sparse. Multi-modal fusion mitigates but does not eliminate this constraint.
2. **Synthetic / controlled data** — All experiments used synthetic sensor streams with known degradation profiles. Real-world noise, sensor drift, and rare failure modes are underrepresented.
3. **Energy savings estimation** — Savings percentages are derived from duty-cycle models rather than continuous power measurement on deployed hardware.
4. **Lead time shortfall** — Peak median lead time reached 9.8 days against a 10-day target. The difference is small but formally means the lead-time criterion was not fully met.
5. **Single industrial domain** — Results are specific to the synthetic sensor-network environment modeled; transfer to other equipment classes is untested.

Future Work Recommendations
- Collect and label additional real acoustic failure events.
- Conduct a field pilot with continuous power metering.
- Explore transfer learning / domain adaptation for new equipment types.
- Investigate online / continual learning to handle concept drift.

Relation to Test Cases
The acoustic underperformance (ANOM-RES-001) is intentionally retained so that analytics and RAG systems can surface the limitation when queried about model weaknesses or experiment anomalies.

headings:
Methodology — Edge ML Predictive Maintenance
**Project:** SYNAPTIX-PM-2023-2025  
**Document ID:** RES-METH-001  
**Version:** 2.1

1. Experimental Design
Ten sequential experiments (EXP-PM-001 to EXP-PM-010) were conducted. Each experiment increased either the feature set, sample size, or model sophistication.

2. Data Collection
Synthetic industrial sensor streams were generated and labeled with failure-imminent flags based on controlled degradation profiles. Sample sizes ranged from 720 to 2,750 per experiment.

3. Model Architecture
- Backbone: quantized 1D CNN + temporal attention (edge-optimized)
- Input windows: 64-timestep sliding windows
- Output: binary probability of failure within next 10 operating days
- Training: 70/15/15 train/val/test splits, stratified

4. Evaluation Metrics
Precision, Recall, F1, False Positive Rate, estimated lead time (median days from first true positive to actual failure event), and modeled energy saving from reduced continuous sensing duty cycle.

5. Anomaly Handling
EXP-PM-006 was retained in the series despite underperformance to document modality limitations. No post-hoc exclusion was applied.

6. Reproducibility
All experiment identifiers, metrics, and the 500-row feature sample (Research_Dataset.csv) are provided for independent verification within the SYNAPTIX COMMAND test environment.
